text:
Maria Gomez: Quick heads-up — seeing a token-level latency spike starting ~10:58. Dashboards show KV prefix cache hit rate for route 'assistant-chat' dropped from ~98% to ~62%. Could be related to the runtime deploy around 10:50. @Tony Li @Kevin Park can you triage? :thinking_face:

Tony Li: I rolled a kernel-selector tweak (prefer_matmul=true) + adjusted batching heuristic to favor latency (shorter batches) in canary at 10:50. Goal was to reduce tail for short chats. I didn't expect major KV-side regressions but possible.

Kevin Park: I also merged a small route-level batching override for 'assistant-chat' in PR #4289 (merged 10:47) that forces batch_timeout=4ms. That could reduce cross-request prefix reuse.

Sara Vasquez: Quick queries to verify numbers — run these in Grafana/Prometheus: 
```
# per-route KV hit rate (5m)
sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total{route="assistant-chat"}[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{route="assistant-chat"}[5m]))

# token latency p95 by stage for assistant-chat
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket{route="assistant-chat"}[5m])) by (le, stage))
```

Maria Gomez: Sampled traces show per-token breakdown skewing toward KV lookup time. Example trace summary (11:02): decode=0.4ms, kv_lookup=1.8ms, kernel_exec=0.9ms, batching_wait=2.1ms (median). Short log snippet:
```
[11:02:12] route=assistant-chat seq_len=120 reuse=0 hits=3 miss=117 kv_lookup=1.9ms
```

Tony Li: Hypothesis: shortening batch windows reduced temporal coalescing of prefixes across requests, so the cache sees more cold lookups. Also kernel selection might pick a kernel layout that's slightly worse for small batched workloads, increasing the relative cost of non-kernel stages.

Kevin Park: We should track a 'kv_reuse_rate' metric (reuse_hits / total_prefix_lookups) per route. I can add a small exporter change to emit it. In the short term we can approximate reuse with a hacky PromQL to get a sense: 
```
(sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total{route="assistant-chat"}[5m])) - sum(rate(kv_cache_prefetch_hits_total{route="assistant-chat"}[5m]))) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{route="assistant-chat"}[5m]))
```
(not perfect but usable for quick triage).

Sara Vasquez: I'll add dashboard panels: 
- 'assistant-chat KV reuse rate (5m)' using Kevin's query
- 'Per-token latency breakdown (decode / kv / kernel / batching)' stacked bar for p50/p95
- Heatmap 'KV reuse by route' (top 20 routes)
Also propose alerts: warn if reuse < 0.85 for 5m, page if reuse < 0.7 for 5m.

deploy-bot: deploy: canary runtime-v1.12.3 (kernel-selector tweak + batching heuristics) at 10:50 - status: success

Maria Gomez: Plan of action: 
1) Rollback the batching override for 'assistant-chat' in canary (Kevin)
2) Add per-route reuse panel + alert (Sara)
3) Re-run kernel-selection off test in canary (Tony)
4) Bisect using a small traffic subset with replay (I will run)

Kevin Park: I'll open PR to revert the override and add a metric shim — targeting PR #4292 in ~30m.

Sara Vasquez: Dashboard patch coming. I'll include GIFs showing how to interpret: eviction spikes vs mem_pressure vs reuse drops. For alerts, suggest severity mapping: warn @channel for <0.85, page on-call for <0.7.

Maria Gomez: For repro, can someone run a synthetic 50 qps test hitting assistant-chat with a long-sequence skew (seq_len ~80-150) to see if we can reproduce the hit-rate collapse? If not, I'll do a production replay.

Tony Li: I'll run a local load job and post the summary here.

observability-bot: new panel added: 'KV reuse by route (5m avg)' - grafana/dashboard/987

Maria Gomez: Thanks all. Keep updates in this thread. If hit rate recovers after Kevin's revert, we can reintroduce kernel tweaks separately and measure impact on reuse and per-token breakdown.
